findings.location: faq[1] 'Should you marry in the USA, in Canada or further abroad?'
findings.issue: States that Australian guests need travel authorisation before flying to the US and Canada. That is the held fact F038/F041 (unconfirmed, Project Lead sign-off) outside an APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF pair. The same answer's UK half is fine (F037, F040).
findings.evidence: "For guests from Australia or the UK, both countries are long-haul and need travel authorisation before flying, so allow more planning time."
findings.suggested_fix: Split it: "For guests from the UK, both countries are long-haul and need travel authorisation before flying (an ESTA or visa for the US, an eTA to fly into Canada). Guests from Australia face the same long-haul trip; [Travel by passport](#entry) shows what to check before booking." Or put the AU clause in its own F038, F041 pair, with a fallback that has no authorisation claim.

findings.location: faq[7] 'Why is a Hawaii wedding not usually all-inclusive?'
findings.issue: The market claim rests only on proposed F049, which comes from doc section 4 addition D. The only source behind that is the named competitor DestinationWeddings.com (D10). It is presented as certain ('Most Hawaii weddings...'), and the question itself asserts it. Under checklist item 7 a competitor cannot be the only source, and an unconfirmed fact cannot appear outside a pair. 'We explain each line before you commit' is also a service promise with no fact id (D3).
findings.evidence: "Most Hawaii weddings are built at luxury hotels that price the ceremony, dinner and rooms separately, rather than sold as one all-inclusive package." / "We explain each line before you commit."
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the question so it makes no claim, and answer without a market claim. For example, Q: "Is a Hawaii wedding all-inclusive?" A: "It can be planned either way. Some couples want one hotel to handle the ceremony, dinner and rooms; others prefer to choose each part separately. Share your guest count and style in the form, and your Wedded Advisor talks you through both routes." Keep F049 out of the copy.

findings.issue: This is an invented business claim (D3). The copy says there are partner venues and suppliers, plural, in both the United States and Canada. The only evidence is the legacy module (F013): Waldorf Astoria (US) and Acamaya Weddings (Mexico, removed under D6). The copywriter's own open question says there is one US listing today, and there is no Canadian listing.
findings.evidence: "Browse partner venues and suppliers in the United States and Canada, and send every enquiry through Wedded Concierge."
findings.suggested_fix: Until the user confirms the route and its listings: "Browse partner venues listed for North America, and send every enquiry through Wedded Concierge." Better still, hide the card (as the CMS note already allows) until 3 or more listings are confirmed. Never name Canada without a Canadian listing.

findings.location: faq[2] 'Where can I get married with just the two of us?'
findings.issue: The answer pairs the Hawaii legal facts with 'just the two of you', which implies a legal Hawaii ceremony needs no witnesses. The witness rule is F029 (unconfirmed, 'Do not state a witness requirement for Hawaii'), so the implication goes beyond the ledger.
findings.evidence: "Hawaii is a strong choice for just the two of you: there is no residency rule, no waiting period once your licence is issued, and you both apply in person together."
findings.suggested_fix: "Hawaii suits a small ceremony: there is no residency rule and no waiting period once your licence is issued. You apply online, then appear together in person, and your Wedded Advisor confirms who else the ceremony needs, such as your licensed officiant."

findings.location: faq[3] 'Is a destination wedding legal in the US?'
findings.issue: This is a general US legal rule stated as fact ('legal when you hold a marriage licence from the state where you marry') with no confirmed fact behind it. Its fact_refs F030, F031 and F032 all read 'Not checked'. The rest of the answer (Hawaii F025/F026, UK F035) is fine.
findings.evidence: "Yes, a wedding in the US is legal when you hold a marriage licence from the state where you marry and follow its rules. Each state sets its own."
findings.suggested_fix: "Yes, when you follow the licence rules of the state where you marry. Each state sets its own, and your Wedded Advisor checks them for your date (D11 wording)." Then add proposed F050 to the ledger and cite it.

findings.issue: 'Quick' implies a fast Nevada licence and no waiting period. Nevada rules are F030 (unconfirmed, blocked), and D11 allows no Las Vegas rule claims without a source. The sentence later says Nevada sets its own rules, which contradicts the speed promise.
findings.evidence: "Las Vegas suits a quick, glamorous ceremony; Nevada sets its own licence rules, and your Wedded Advisor checks them before you book flights."
findings.suggested_fix: "Las Vegas suits a glamorous chapel or hotel ceremony; Nevada sets its own licence rules, and your Wedded Advisor checks them before you book flights."

findings.issue: The scenery is stated plainly, but it rests on proposed F048, which is research-doc tier from third-party listicles. Stronger sources exist (tourism board tier ranks above the research doc in source_of_truth_order). The claims are low risk and descriptive, with no prices, capacities or legal points, so this is not a blocker. F048 should still be checked against tourism board pages before publishing.
findings.evidence: "On the Big Island, black sand beaches and lava fields meet the sea." / "A grand hotel above a lake that freezes in winter" / "a second line follows the couple out of the ceremony, with a brass band and guests waving handkerchiefs"
findings.suggested_fix: No copy change needed if F048 is confirmed against gohawaii.com (Maui resort coasts, Big Island black sand), banfflakelouise.com or pc.gc.ca (Lake Louise freezing in winter), neworleans.com (second line) and explorecharleston.com (live oaks). Until then, list F048 as unconfirmed in NOTES.md.

findings.issue: 'Your one contact' is a service promise that goes beyond F021, which says the advisor 'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance', not that they are the only contact. brand-answers has no approved row for it (D3). It has no fact id.
findings.evidence: "Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact: they explain your options..." / "Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact for places, venues, legal steps and guest travel"
findings.suggested_fix: "Your Wedded Advisor plans with you throughout: they explain your options..." and "Your Wedded Advisor helps with places, venues, legal steps and guest travel". Or get a brand-answers row approved for a single point of contact.

findings.location: s3-compare table rows Aspen, Charleston, Banff and Lake Louise; s1 and s3 'every other state and province'
findings.issue: 'Rules set by Colorado', 'Rules set by South Carolina' and 'Rules set by Alberta' have no fact id. F031 covers California, F032 New York, F030 Nevada, and F034 lists only BC, Quebec and Ontario. The wording follows D11, but the ledger has no general 'each state or province sets its own rules' fact.
findings.evidence: "| Aspen | Mountains | Rules set by Colorado; we check them for your date |" / "| Banff and Lake Louise | ... | Rules set by Alberta; we check them for your date |"
findings.suggested_fix: No copy change. Ledger fixes: (a) add proposed F050 (licence rules are set by each US state and each Canadian province) and cite it on these rows, in s1 and in the 'Every other state and province' paragraph; (b) Project Lead to extend F034's value to cover Alberta.

findings.location: faq[0] 'Where is the most popular wedding destination in the United States?'
findings.issue: The superlative search claim is not supported by the cited facts. F008 (Hawaii 880, US) is compared only with F007 terms. The US volume for 'las vegas wedding' is not in the ledger (F009 is AU only), so 'more searches than any other US wedding destination we track' cannot be shown, and it reads as a market-wide claim.
findings.evidence: "Hawaii draws more searches than any other US wedding destination we track, but the right place depends on your style."
findings.suggested_fix: "Hawaii is one of the most searched US wedding destinations, but the right place depends on your style." (F008, 880 a month in the US), or drop the search claim: "There is no single answer: the right place depends on your style."

findings.issue: 'Simplest' is a comparative claim. The ledger supports the Hawaii facts (F025, F026) but not a ranking against other states.
findings.evidence: "Hawaii is the simplest legal example: no residency rule, and no waiting period once your licence is issued."
findings.suggested_fix: "Take Hawaii as the legal example: no residency rule, and no waiting period once your licence is issued."

findings.issue: 'Few regions change this much in one flight' is an unsupported comparison. Hawaii to Banff is not normally one flight.
findings.evidence: "Few regions change this much in one flight."
findings.suggested_fix: "Few regions change this much from one place to the next." or cut the sentence.

findings.issue: Presenting no residency rule and no waiting period as unique to Hawaii overstates F025/F026, which make no comparison with other places.
findings.evidence: "Only here ... A legal Hawaii marriage with no residency rule and no waiting period once your licence is issued."
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the list 'Why couples choose it', or keep 'Only here' and swap this item for a scenery line (for example, black sand beaches on the Big Island).

findings.issue: 'Apply in person together' is not accurate. F024 says you apply online, then both partners meet the agent together in person.
findings.evidence: "you both apply in person together"
findings.suggested_fix: "you apply online, then appear together in person" (covered by the FC-M1 fix).

findings.issue: 'No authorisation' is broader than F043, which says no tourist visa under 180 days and still requires a passport, passport card or NEXUS. The ledger does not state an eTA exemption for US citizens.
findings.evidence: "US guests need no authorisation to visit Canada for stays under 180 days."
findings.suggested_fix: "US guests need no tourist visa to visit Canada for stays under 180 days; fly on a US passport."

findings.issue: It leaves out the VWP condition in F037 (unrestricted right of abode in the UK). This is optional, but it is the one condition that changes the answer for some UK passport holders.
findings.evidence: "UK passports: an ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program, or a visa, before travel to the US"
findings.suggested_fix: Add: "(the Visa Waiver Program needs an unrestricted right of abode in the UK)".

findings.issue: 'For your dates and hotel' suggests Privileges benefits linked to hotels. D3 allows no Privileges benefits until brand-answers row 7 is approved.
findings.evidence: "Wedded Privileges: ask your Wedded Advisor what the programme offers for your dates and hotel."
findings.suggested_fix: "Wedded Privileges: ask your Wedded Advisor what the programme offers."

findings.issue: The Studio feature list (travel times, rooms, dress codes, plans for children) goes beyond F023, which says only that there is a guest website. 'One advisor plans the whole celebration' strengthens F021.
findings.evidence: "Give your guests one place for travel times, rooms, dress codes and plans for children." / "One advisor plans the whole celebration with you"
findings.suggested_fix: "Give your guests one website for your plans." and "A Wedded Advisor plans with you, from the first call to the guest list."

findings.issue: 'The legal ... steps for US, UK and AU passports' overstates the page. Full legal steps are given only for Hawaii (and the NYC appointment rule); AU entry is held.
findings.evidence: "with the legal and travel steps for US, UK and AU passports"
findings.suggested_fix: "with Hawaii's licence steps and travel rules for US, UK and AU passports" (matches meta.description).

findings.issue: The fallback suggests all legal rules come from official sites. Only Hawaii (F024 to F028) and the NYC rule (F033) do; the other states and provinces are hedged.
findings.evidence: "[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] Legal and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026."
findings.suggested_fix: "[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] Hawaii licence steps and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026."

findings.issue: 'The places couples ask about most' is a demand claim, so it needs the keyword facts as refs. Only F009 is cited.
findings.evidence: "Hawaii, California and the places couples ask about most"
findings.suggested_fix: Add F006, F007 and F008 to s2 fact_refs; the wording is acceptable under D10.

findings.issue: 'A Wedded Advisor replies' is a reply promise. F020 confirms routing to Wedded Concierge, not who replies.
findings.evidence: "A Wedded Advisor replies."
findings.suggested_fix: "Every enquiry goes to Wedded Concierge."

proposed_facts.fact: Marriage licence rules set by each US state and Canadian province
proposed_facts.value: Marriage licence rules are set by each US state (many issue licences at county level) and by each Canadian province; there is no single national licence process

proposed_facts.notes: New entry proposed by the fact checker to back the D11 hedge wording ('Rules set by <state or province>') in s1, s3 and FAQ 4 and 5. It states no state-specific rule. Not fetched (fast mode).

assumptions: In fast mode, no web fetches were made. No new legal claim needed one; F050 was proposed with a URL to check instead.
D11's hedge wording ('Rules set by <state or province>') is treated as allowed, and the missing fact id behind it as a major finding, not a blocker.
Holding F046 proof numbers in a sign-off pair is treated as compliant with D3, since they come from brand-answers row 6 and are not invented.
F021 is used as D3 directs, even though the ledger lists Project Lead sign-off.
The descriptive scenery (F048) needs no sign-off pair; it is marked major for source tier, not as an unconfirmed fact stated as certain.
